species.name: Striped bass
why: Water 65°F on top, right in their comfort range.
Best water today is 8–22 ft deep, mostly on channel edges.
The lake is layered: warm water down to about 60 ft, cold below.
Little oxygen below about 95 ft, so fish stay above it.
Northwest wind at 15 mph pushes bait onto the southeast shore: try the wind-blown banks.

species.name: White bass
why: Water 65°F on top, a bit cool for them, so they feed in the warmest water they can find.
Best water today is 8–20 ft deep, mostly on open water over the deep basin.
The lake is layered: warm water down to about 60 ft, cold below.
Little oxygen below about 95 ft, so fish stay above it.
Northwest wind at 15 mph pushes bait onto the southeast shore: try the wind-blown banks.

species.name: Catfish
why: Water 65°F on top, much colder than they like, so they move slowly and stay deep.
